description: Text a migration must quote rather than mangle: single and double quotes, backslashes, newlines and tabs, non-ASCII and emoji, and an empty string beside a NULL.
schema: CREATE TABLE t (id int PRIMARY KEY, v text);
before: INSERT INTO t VALUES (1, 'plain'), (2, 'to be deleted'), (3, NULL);
after: INSERT INTO t VALUES (1, E'it''s a "quote" and a back\\slash'), (3, ''), (4, E'line1\nline2\ttab'), (5, 'ünïcödé 🎉'), (6, E'trailing backslash \\');
compare: SELECT id, v, v IS NULL FROM t ORDER BY id

description: json and jsonb holding quotes, backslashes, nesting, a bare string and a JSON null — distinct from an SQL NULL.
schema: CREATE TABLE j (id int PRIMARY KEY, a json, b jsonb);
before: INSERT INTO j VALUES (1, '{"k": 1}', '{"k": 1}'), (2, NULL, NULL);
after: INSERT INTO j VALUES (1, '{"q": "it''s \"quoted\"", "n": [1, {"x": null}]}', '{"q": "back\\slash", "z": true}'), (2, '"just a string"', 'null'), (3, '[]', '{}');
compare: SELECT id, a::text, b::text, a IS NULL, b IS NULL FROM j ORDER BY id

description: Arrays whose elements need quoting — commas, braces, quotes, spaces — with NULL elements, an empty array and a two-dimensional one.
schema: CREATE TABLE a (id int PRIMARY KEY, t text[], m int[]);
after: INSERT INTO a VALUES (1, ARRAY['a,b', '{c}', 'd"e', 'f g', NULL, ''], '{{1,2},{3,4}}'), (2, '{}', NULL);
compare: SELECT id, t::text, m::text FROM a ORDER BY id

description: bytea, including a zero byte, high bytes and an empty value. A driver may hand these back as a stream rather than a string.
schema: CREATE TABLE b (id int PRIMARY KEY, v bytea);
compare: SELECT id, encode(v, 'hex') FROM b ORDER BY id

description: Values that lose something if they pass through a float or an unquoted literal: high-precision numerics, NaN and infinities, the smallest double, and bigint at both ends.
schema: CREATE TABLE n (id int PRIMARY KEY, d numeric, f float8, i bigint);
compare: SELECT id, d::text, f::text, i::text FROM n ORDER BY id

description: timestamptz written in other zones, infinite timestamps and dates, intervals with months and seconds, and a time with a zone.
schema: CREATE TABLE tm (id int PRIMARY KEY, ts timestamptz, d date, iv interval, tz timetz);
compare: SELECT id, ts AT TIME ZONE 'UTC', d::text, iv::text, tz::text FROM tm ORDER BY id

description: A two-column primary key: rows updated, inserted and deleted by both parts of the key, one of which shares a value with another row.
schema: CREATE TABLE c (a int, b text, v text, PRIMARY KEY (a, b));
compare: SELECT a, b, v FROM c ORDER BY a, b

description: A table with no key at all, holding duplicate rows. Rows can only be told apart by their values, and a duplicate counts.
schema: CREATE TABLE k (x int, y text);
compare: SELECT x, y, count(*) FROM k GROUP BY x, y ORDER BY x, y

description: Rows in a table whose key is GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY: inserting them with their ids needs OVERRIDING SYSTEM VALUE.
schema: CREATE TABLE ia (id int GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY, v text);
after: INSERT INTO ia (id, v) OVERRIDING SYSTEM VALUE VALUES (1, 'first'), (7, 'seventh');
compare: SELECT id, v FROM ia ORDER BY id

description: A table with a stored generated column. Its values follow from the others: a migration writing them is refused by the server.
schema: CREATE TABLE g (id int PRIMARY KEY, a int, twice int GENERATED ALWAYS AS (a * 2) STORED);
compare: SELECT id, a, twice FROM g ORDER BY id

description: Columns typed by an enum and by a domain over text.
schema: CREATE TYPE mood AS ENUM ('sad', 'ok', 'happy'); CREATE DOMAIN code AS text CHECK (VALUE ~ '^[A-Z]+$'); CREATE TABLE ed (id int PRIMARY KEY, m mood, c code);
compare: SELECT id, m::text, c::text FROM ed ORDER BY id

description: uuid, boolean, inet, macaddr, bit strings, money and a range.
schema: CREATE TABLE at (id int PRIMARY KEY, u uuid, ok boolean, ip inet, mac macaddr, bits bit varying(8), price money, r int4range);
before: INSERT INTO at VALUES (1, NULL, false, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL);
compare: SELECT id, u::text, ok::text, ip::text, mac::text, bits::text, price::numeric::text, r::text FROM at ORDER BY id
